name: Smashed lamp claim
blurb: Furious, sarcastic, cuts the notice off
title: A smashed lamp and a forty pound limit
summary: A furious caller gives her tracking number in her first breath and cuts the agent off when it starts the claims notice. The agent has to finish the notice anyway. She answers the forty pound limit with sarcasm: an agent that takes it as a yes, tells her to calm down or asks for the tracking number again loses her to a chargeback.

golden.scenario: Caller's lamp arrived smashed and she wants compensation.
golden.expected_outcome: The agent does not ask for the tracking number again. The agent says photos are needed and the packaging must be kept before taking claim details, even after being cut off. The limit is said as 'forty pounds', her sarcasm is not taken as acceptance, and she is told the retailer can claim the full value. A claim for the £320 lamp and a fragile-handling complaint are both logged, with a decision due by Wednesday 19 August.

agent_setup.knowledge: Std. cover: max. £40.00/parcel. Sender (retailer) may claim full value. Claim decision: 5 working days.

metrics.name: Upset Caller
metrics.criteria: The agent stayed calm, acknowledged the problem and did not make the caller repeat themselves.

metrics.name: Required Disclosure
metrics.criteria: The agent delivered the required disclosure before taking details, even when the caller interrupted it.

metrics.name: Prosodic Cues
metrics.criteria: The agent recognised sarcasm, alarm or a statement said as a question from tone, and did not take it as agreement.

metrics.name: Text Normalization
metrics.criteria: The agent said prices, units, titles and abbreviations the way a person would say them.
